pr_comments:
RE: commit messages

Try to provide a descriptive subject line for each commit. Putting `[Requested Changes]` forces someone later on to have to dig into the full message. Commit messages provide a history of the code base and are invaluable when performing analysis and trying to understand how/why a piece of code evolved the way it did. Also, in general, commit messages should answer _why_ and not _what_ -- the diff will always provide the _what_changed, but the _why_ is often lost and turns out to be the more important piece of information months or years down the line when someone else comes in and tries to understand the code.

<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->

Create an IOrderBook interface and maybe DefaultOrderBook class to cover basic needs.
